subject: Hospitality
title: Brand Segmentation
description: Learn Brand Segmentation in one minute.

hook.text: Marriott owns 30+ hotel brands—from Ritz-Carlton to Fairfield Inn. One company, every price point.

buildup.text: Each brand targets a specific traveler: luxury, lifestyle, business, extended stay, budget. The parent owns them all.

discovery.text: Segmentation ensures a guest never leaves the portfolio. Outgrow Courtyard? Move to Marriott. Want luxury? Try Ritz.

twist.text: Too many brands cause 'brand confusion.' Guests can't tell Aloft from Element from AC Hotels. Differentiation blurs.

climax.text: The strategy is borrowed from car companies: GM had Chevrolet to Cadillac. Marriott runs the same playbook with beds.

punchline.text: Thirty brands, one company, every wallet size. Hospitality is a portfolio.

quiz.question: Why do hotel companies own so many different brands?
options: To cover every price point and keep guests in the portfolio
Each brand serves a different country
